LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Seattle has struggled a bit on offense, as Sam Darnold has not looked as sharp as he did last season. Darnold had a glute injury in Week 1 that sidelined him for a game, but he has started three games in a row for Seattle, leading it to a 1-2 record. Seattle still remains an elite defensive team, ranking No. 1 in the league in yards per play allowed and EPA/Play this season. Bo Nix is really struggling in his third NFL season, and Denver is averaging the seventh-fewest yards per play (4.7) in the NFL. Denver and Seattle both have playoff expectations – and Super Bowl hopes – in the 2026 season, but their offenses have to improve to make those dreams a reality. With Denver banged up a bit in the secondary on Thursday, Seattle has a shot to get back on track. It won’t be easy, though, as the Broncos are 2-0 at home with impressive victories against Jacksonville and the Los Angeles Rams. away.headline: Broncos-Seahawks report card: Once again, Denver defense bails out offense in win
away.blurb: After two long scoring drives that were a perfect blend of the pass and run, Denver’s offense was invisible in the second half. The Broncos gained two first downs, posted 30 yards, did not score and went three-and-out four times. They gained 32 yards on their last 10 drives, including penalties. It was a completely lackluster effort that wasted a defensive gem. If this is what Vance Joseph’s defense can look like without two All-Pro-caliber players in the secondary, watch out, AFC. Denver’s defense has put together multiple excellent games, but Thursday night was the unit’s watershed showing. Broncos' Jonathon Cooper removed from exempt list, available to play Week 7 On the boundary, the Broncos barely missed a beat despite Pat Surtain II being out with an ankle injury and Riley Moss barely playing because of a rib injury. Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron kept Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in front of them for the most part and held Seattle’s other options in check. Seahawks returner Rashid Shaheed did have a huge kickoff return and a few nice punt returns, though. But what if you told them it would look like this: 2.9 yards per play, 3-of-14 on third down, a third-year quarterback rapidly regressing and an offense that's allergic to explosive plays. That's the conundrum in Denver right now, where the Broncos keep finding ways to win ugly. Thursday was a reversal of the typical Broncos . Strong first half, dismal showing in the second. Bo Nix’s struggles are bordering on outright disasters at this point. away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. Guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) went from being listed as limited Monday to full participation Tuesday, while every other player's status stayed the same. home.headline: Broncos-Seahawks report card: Once again, Denver defense bails out offense in win
home.blurb: After two long scoring drives that were a perfect blend of the pass and run, Denver’s offense was invisible in the second half. The Broncos gained two first downs, posted 30 yards, did not score and went three-and-out four times. They gained 32 yards on their last 10 drives, including penalties. It was a completely lackluster effort that wasted a defensive gem. If this is what Vance Joseph’s defense can look like without two All-Pro-caliber players in the secondary, watch out, AFC. Denver’s defense has put together multiple excellent games, but Thursday night was the unit’s watershed showing. Broncos' Jonathon Cooper removed from exempt list, available to play Week 7 On the boundary, the Broncos barely missed a beat despite Pat Surtain II being out with an ankle injury and Riley Moss barely playing because of a rib injury. Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron kept Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in front of them for the most part and held Seattle’s other options in check. Seahawks returner Rashid Shaheed did have a huge kickoff return and a few nice punt returns, though. But what if you told them it would look like this: 2.9 yards per play, 3-of-14 on third down, a third-year quarterback rapidly regressing and an offense that's allergic to explosive plays. That's the conundrum in Denver right now, where the Broncos keep finding ways to win ugly. Thursday was the latest example, as Denver defeated the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 on “Thursday Night Football” at Empower Field. Here's The Denver Post's report card from Thursday night . Thursday was a reversal of the typical Broncos . Strong first half, dismal showing in the second. Bo Nix’s struggles are bordering on outright disasters at this point. He threw for just 107 yards on 17 completions — a strikingly low 6.3 yards per completion. A week after one of the worst games of his career, Nix followed it up with his fifth-lowest total. Denver’s wideouts are struggling to get open, as well. And while the run game showed flashes in the first half, it still finished with 2.6 yards per carry. J.K. Dobbins rushed for just 6 yards on six carries in the second half. The Broncos keep winning these games, but eventually their offense will need to hold up its end of the bargain. Every level of Denver’s defense played excellent football. The Broncos’ pass rush relentlessly attacked Sam Darnold from the interior and the edge. The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Jaguars sign Jacob Bobenmoyer to practice squad after Matiscik injury Jacob Bobenmoyer will take over snapping duties after DaVon Hamilton's emergency stint, per report. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. You can follow him on X (formerly Twitter) at @Demetrius82 or on Bluesky at Demetrius .

away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3). away.headline: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Latest Return Timeline for Bears QB
away.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is inactive for Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers but has a chance to return in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that Williams "could return sometime in the next several weeks." Williams practiced Friday on a limited basis and Bears head coach Ben Johnson addresses his recovery: The Bears selected Williams, a former Oklahoma and USC star, with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft. He and the Bears broke out in 2025, the first season under head coach Ben Johnson. Chicago won the NFC North and reached the NFC Divisional round thanks in part due to Williams' late-game heroics. He ended up throwing for 3,942 passing yards and 27 touchdowns. Still, Pelissero suggested Chicago is willing to be patient with his recovery. The NFL insider cited the Bears' next two games (Oct. 18 against the Falcons and Oct. 22 against the New England Patriots) as possible occasions for him to be activated. They'll have a long turnaround between Weeks 7 and 8, 11 days, which would afford Williams more time to recuperate and sharpen up if he needs it. The third-year signal-caller began his 2026 season with an explosive performance during a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 269 yards and two touchdowns while adding 65 rushing yards and two more scores. Unfortunately, Williams suffered a Grade 2 right hamstring strain while he was running for the end zone in the fourth quarter of the Bears' Week 2 game against the Minnesota Vikings (9-3 loss). Williams fell to the ground on the six-yard line on a non-contact play and was stretchered off the field. ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Sept. 27 that the injury could sideline him for "three-to-four weeks." Without Williams, Tyson Bagent is the team's interim starter, and Case Keenum is the backup. Keenum starred in Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles in a 27-7 win after Bagent missed most of practice leading to the game ( concussion protocol ). He finished with 247 passing yards and two touchdowns. Bagent took over the following week and led the Bears to a 23-12 win (268 passing yards).

Williams' return in Week 6 felt like a sure-thing ever since he landed on last Friday's injury report as 'Questionable', but now it's confirmed. Caleb Williams Reposts Electric Hype Video Hinting at Return For Bears vs. Falcons This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/bears/onsi as Bears' Caleb Williams Makes Official Return from Injury in Week 6 vs Falcons . For the first time since Week 2, the Chicago Bears will finally have their starting quarterback under center. According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo , Caleb Williams has passed all the tests for his injured hamstring and is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Though Bears fans widely expected Williams to be back after a full week of practice, and especially after he reposted an electric hype video on social media, it has to feel good to get this official confirmation. The Bears went 2-1 in Williams' absence, a good record for any team to hit without their starting quarterback, but a disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers reminded everyone just how badly Williams is missed. Between Williams wanting to remind the NFL world of who he is and sheer necessity, I would hate to be the Falcons' defense tomorrow. home.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out
away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about the defender, saying he is excited to get him back out on the field. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up for their divisional matchup with their former offensive coordinator-turned-head coach, Todd Monken, and his Cleveland Browns. The full final injury report is as follows: Jackson is still dealing with his sprained ankle and will now miss his second consecutive game. Joining Jackson is rookie tight end Matt Hibner, who suffered a hand injury. Reports indicate that Hibner has a cast on his hand, pointing to what could be a significant injury. There are no other red flags unless Jones or Vorhees are both unable to play, which would put the Baltimore offensive line in a very tough spot.

away.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. home.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
home.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. home.headline: Browns Get Optimistic Injury Outlook Ahead of Week 6
home.blurb: The defensive duo of Mason Graham and Carson Schwesinger both returned to the practice field for the first time this week, on Friday. They both share a questionable game status heading into the weekend, but it's certainly a step in the right direction toward both suiting up against Baltimore. Graham has been dealing with knee and ankle ailments dating back to Cleveland's Thursday night win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4. The injuries kept him out of commission for last week's loss to the New York Jets, but could be poised to make a critical return. As for Schwesinger, he was seen leaving the locker room in New York in a walking boot and has been nursing an ankle injury this week. The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year dealt with a similar situation last season, where he didn't practice the first two days of the week, then was limited for a Friday practice and wound up playing against the Jets two days later. Joining Graham and Schwesinger as questionable is star running back Quinshon Judkins, who has also been battling an ankle injury this week. He too returned to practice on Friday after missing the previous two days. Fellow running back Dylan Sampson has also been ramping things up after an IR stint this week. Sampson was limited on Thursday and Friday, but was ruled out. DE Derek Barnett, who is dealing with an ankle injury, is also listed as questionable. Two active players were officially ruled out in DT Mike Hall Jr (ankle) and G Teven Jenkins, who has missed each of the first five weeks of the season due to a back injury. DT Kalia Davis has been ruled out, as well. He spent the first four weeks on the IR, then had his 21-day practice window opened last week, but has only practiced once since then. Similarly, Dillon Gabriel has practiced every day since returning to practice off the IR ahead of Week 5, but also won't be activated this week. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. We move on to the Week 6 slate, and three writers have their upset picks locked in. Let's dive into them. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. The Indianapolis Colts return home to host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Oct. 18, with Indy favored by nearly a touchdown despite some concerning underlying metrics. TOP Pick Titans vs Colts prediction: Titans +6.5 It's ugly, but I'd trade the Tennessee Titans +6.5, down to +5.5 , against the Indianapolis Colts . This is more of an anti-Indianapolis pick than pro-Tennessee. The Colts are 31st in net yards per play, 29th in early-down EPA per play differential, and 32nd in net quarterback pressure rate. I know the Titans suck, but should any team with that type of profile be a 6.5-point favorite? Also, after starting out last season hot, his first in Indianapolis, QB Daniel Jones is back to being terrible . Jones is 24th in adjusted EPA per play, according to RBSDM.com , and 26th in QBR. Titans vs Colts combo A Tennessee cover should correlate with an ugly, lower-scoring game, so I'm pairing Titans +6.5 with Under 44.5 and RB Tony Pollard 60+ rushing yards. Tennessee needs to shorten this game and keep QB Cam Ward out of obvious passing situations. That means establishing the run with Pollard against an Indianapolis defense ranked 27th in yards per rush allowed . That ground-heavy approach helps the Under. Neither offense has been trustworthy on late downs, and Tennessee and Indianapolis are tied for 24th in third-down conversion rate. A competitive game featuring long possessions, field goals, and limited explosive passing plays is exactly what I'm looking for. Tony Pollard Over 59.5 rushing yards Titans vs Colts touchdown scorer: Carnell Tate I'd trade Carnell Tate 's anytime touchdown probability up to 30%. Tate, the first receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at No. 4 overall, is overdue for his first score. He has 37 targets this season, and Atlanta's Drake London is the only other pass-catcher with at least 37 targets who still doesn't have a receiving touchdown. The matchup also helps. All five Indianapolis starting defensive backs have failing PFF grades , while the Colts rank 22nd in defensive dropback EPA per play, according to RBSDM.com. If there's ever a spot for Tate to finally break through, this is it. home.headline: Colts Announce Roster Move Amid Tyler Warren Injury Uncertainty
home.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts activated tight end Will Mallory from injured reserve on Saturday ahead of Sunday's home game against the Tennessee Titans . The team also confirmed that his questionable designation has been lifted, clearing him to play. Starting tight end Tyler Warren is listed as questionable with a groin injury that limited him in Friday's practice. Reports indicated that Warren was visibly uncomfortable after aggravating the issue during the portion of practice open to the media. If Warren cannot go, the Colts' passing attack loses its most reliable target at the position. That is where Mallory steps in. The former fifth-round pick out of Miami has shown the ability to contribute as a receiver when given opportunities, and his preseason performance before the injury suggested he was ready for a bigger role. The receiving corps is stretched thin beyond the tight end position. Alec Pierce remains out. Ashton Dulin has been ruled out for the fourth straight game with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies is also out with a rib issue he sustained during the team's London game. Indianapolis has struggled to generate consistent production through the air this season, and losing Warren for any amount of time would only compound the problem. Having Mallory available gives the Colts at least one additional option they did not have a week ago. Colts Announce Roster Move Amid Tyler Warren Injury Uncertainty Unlock the latest Heavy on Colts news — direct to your inbox. Mallory has not appeared in a game this season after suffering a thumb injury during the preseason. He has spent the first five weeks on injured reserve, and the Colts opened his 21-day practice window earlier this month to begin the process of bringing him back. Mallory led all Colts pass catchers in the team's preseason opener against the Patriots , hauling in six receptions for 80 yards. The production was there. The health was not. Now both appear to be in place. INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – OCTOBER 20: Will Mallory #86 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to a game against the Miami Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 20, 2024 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) What the Colts Are Dealing With on Offense Getty Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren Mallory is back. Whether he steps into a featured role or a complementary one depends on Warren's availability Sunday morning. Either way, a passing game that has been searching for answers just got one more option. The Colts will look to respond against Cam Ward and the Titans. I'm not sure I'm ready to back them to cover a 7.5-point spread against a division rival this week. Pick: Jets +7.5 (-115) via FanDuel I think I disagree with MacMillan on this one. The Patriots have put up two dominating wins in their first two home games. They beat the Steelers 20-3 as -4.5 favorites in Week 2 and covered as just -3.5 favorites in the blowout last week. The Jets may be able to keep this from being a complete blowout, but I think the Patriots can pull away at home. New York has failed to cover in both of its road losses. picks.headline: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: New England Patriots
picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: New England Patriots - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Auburn stuns No. 1 Georgia A.J. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: New England Patriots EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 28: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball against the New York Jets during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on December 28, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Pamela Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double Sat, October 17, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets find themselves in a familiar position heading into Sunday's game in New England. If they could just find a way to upset the Patriots, it change the direction of their season and start to see them considered as a force to be reckoned with in the AFC. Could this be the time when they finally achieve that, or will they be hanging on to relevance by a thread once again after Sunday? Let's break down the Patriots' roster going position by position: Drake Maye is coming off a season where he was a legitimate MVP candidate. However, after three weeks, he wasn't playing like that. The Patriots were 1-2 as Maye had thrown six interceptions and just one touchdown pass. However, he's rediscovered himself over the past two games, leading New England to a come-from-behind win against the Bills and a blowout of the Raiders. His 374 yard output against the Raiders represented the second-highest total of his career, as he completed multiple deep balls. Over the two wins, he had seven touchdowns and just one interception. The Patriots' number two is Tommy DeVito, who won three straight games as an undrafted rookie with the Giants but hasn't had much success since then. Seventh round rookie Behren Morton is the number three. Offensive Line New England has a question mark on their offensive line this week after left tackle Will Campbell was injured and knocked out of the previous game. Campbell has been practicing on a limited basis all week but his game status is uncertain and he's listed as questionable. In last week's game, first round pick Caleb Lomu stepped in for Campbell and did well. In college, Lomu faced David Bailey and handled him well, although this was while Bailey was still at Stanford, so he hadn't fully broken out yet. New England has multiple ex-Jets on their offensive line with Morgan Moses at right tackle and Alijah Vera-Tucker at left guard. They also have Greg Van Roten, but he's on injured reserve. The 35-year old Moses is doing a solid job, although he does have five penalties in five games. So far, the injury-prone Vera-Tucker has been completely healthy with the Patriots. The other starters are last year's third round pick Jared Wilson at center and veteran Mike Onwenu at right guard. However, Onwenu is also on injured reserve, so Ben Brown is currently starting there. Matt Pryor, Walter Rouse and sixth round rookie Dametrious Crownover are available as cover. Rouse already had to fill in for 41 snaps in week three. In the event of an injury to Wilson, Brown would probably slide across to center. Running Backs Similar to Campbell, running back TreVeyon Henderson has practiced on a limited basis this week but his status is uncertain after he picked up a high ankle sprain in last week's game. He has said he feels pretty good but has been listed as questionable with New England also perhaps thinking ahead to their matchup with the Bears next Thursday. Henderson had 900 yards and nine touchdowns last year, but Rhamondre Stevenson is a more than adequate replacement, who has been a thousand-yard back in the past. He leads the team in rushing yards so far this year. The number three is Corey Kiner, who saw some playing time last week but fumbled once. Pass catchers The Patriots activated AJ Brown for practice this week, after he had been injured in the opener, so he may return to give their offense a further boost on Sunday, although his official game status is questionable. In Brown's absence, Mack Hollins had been leading the team in receptions, but he is also now on injured reserve. Offseason signing Romeo Doubs leads the team with 219 receiving yards and Pop Douglas is coming off a game last week where he caught two touchdown passes. Slot receiver Efton Chism is now a regular part of the rotation and responded with the winning touchdown against the Bills on a spectacular one-handed catch. Kyle Williams also gets regular playing time and has been established as a big play threat. At tight end, Hunter Henry is off to a modest start, having caught 60 passes with seven touchdowns last year. Third round rookie Eli Raridon is the number two, and has eight catches with a touchdown, while Tanner Arkin and Cameron Latu are also on the roster with Julian Hill on injured reserve. Defensive Line The starters on the defensive line are former first round pick Christian Barmore, nose tackle Cory Durden and last year's big money signing Milton Williams, who had 3.5 sacks. DaQuan Jones gives them an experienced backup at the nose tackle position with Joshua Farmer and ex-Jet Leonard Taylor III also on the team. All six of these players were active in the Raiders game, although Taylor has played the least on defense. New England are without their top two pass rushers from last season, as K'Lavon Chaisson left during the offseason and Harold Landry is on the PUP list. These two combined for 16 sacks last season. In their place, the starters on the edge are Elijah Ponder and Dre'Mont Jones, with Ponder having really stepped up so far as he has 4.5 sacks and leads the team in quarterback hits and tackles for loss. Second round rookie Gabe Jacas is likely to see his role continue to expand though, as he's flashed playmaking abilities as a rotational player with 1.5 sacks, an interception, three tackles for loss and five quarterback hits. The inside linebackers are led by Robert Spillane, who had 97 tackles last season and is leading the team again in that category. Alongside him, Christian Elliss also plays a full time role. Elliss is another Patriots player who is listed as questionable, although he practiced full on Friday. The reserves on the inside are Erick Hunter, Darius Muasau and sixth round rookie Namdi Obiazor, although they don't play much. All three got some valuable reps in garbage time last week though. Defensive Backs New England has some real talent at cornerback with their three starters all having posted double digits for passes defensed last year. Former first round pick Christian Gonzalez was a pro bowler and the slot cornerback Marcus Jones intercepted three passes last year to prove he's not just a punt returner. Carlton Davis was a big money signing who slotted well into the rotation. Davis has been ruled out due to injury and Gonzalez also had some injury issues, but he appears to be good to go. The main backup is Charles Woods, so he may need to step in for Davis. Fifth round rookie Karon Prunty, Channing Canada and Kindle Vildor are the other backups, but Prunty has been ruled out and Canada is listed as questionable. At safety New England brought in Kevin Byard to replace Jaylinn Hawkins, who had led them with four interceptions in 2025. Craig Woodson returns as the other starter with Dell Pettus on injured reserve. Woodson is also listed as questionable but was not limited in practice on Friday, so should be fine to play. Jaylen Reed has also started one game and seen action in three-safety sets, while Mike Brown is available in reserve and Brenden Schooler is mostly just a special teamer. Special Teams Kicker Andy Borregales missed seven kicks last season and has already missed two this year. He had the game winner against the Bills last season and also had the game-winner against Denver in the AFC title game, albeit in the third quarter. Punter Brian Baringer is on injured reserve so veteran Mitch Wishnowsky currently has this role. He has a net average of below 40 yards but has only allowed 64 return yards. In the return game, Jones is a two-time all pro as a punt returner and once had the game winning score against the Jets (albeit due to an obvious missed holding penalty). He had two more touchdowns last year. Douglas is listed as his backup, while Williams handles kickoffs with Chism as his number two. The pro bowler Schooler has only played one game so far this year, but the Patriots have plenty of other productive players in kick coverage, including Elliss, Ponder, Obiazor, Hunter and Muasau. The backup cornerbacks share the gunner roles along with Schooler.

New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit New Orleans Saints Predictions Turn Heads on New York Giants Game Joey Hickey Sun, October 18, 2026 at 1:47 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints (1-4) get set to take on the New York Giants (3-1-1) on Sunday. The game gives the Saints an opportunity to take on what may end up a division winner in the NFC East. The game presents a shot at a morale-boosting win and one that the Saints could build on to get out of their current rut. The Giants, however, do not intend to go down that easily. ESPN NFL insider Katherine Terrell shared the latest on the Saints heading into the matchup. Here's some of what Terrell wrote alongside other ESPN experts. There's frustration to go around after the Saints' third straight loss, and owner Gayle Benson made a rare public statement commenting on how the team's current record is not acceptable. QB Tyler Shough says he understands and shares her frustration. "She wasn't saying anything that wasn't already known, and she did a really good job of highlighting the expectations, and we have those same expectations for ourselves," he said. -- Fellow ESPN NFL insider Jordan Raanan gave intel on the Giants. Here's some of what Raanan had to say. "The Giants are playing at home and became underdogs as the week progressed. That didn't seem to sit well with the team. 'We love playing at MetLife Stadium and being underdogs,' defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said. 'Everybody counts us out.' The Giants are admittedly playing with a chip on their shoulders after RB Cam Skattebo said it was dumb for them to be underdogs in their previous home game against the Cardinals." Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints offensive coordinator Doug Nussmeier looks one against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The analysis drew mixed results from the ESPN panel, but two of the three analysts who predicted the game took the Saints to win the game. In a noteworthy prediction, Seth Walder had the Saints winning the game 20-14. If the Saints can hold an opponent to 14 points, it would be a huge win for the defensive unit. New Orleans held the Minnesota Vikings to 23 points in a 23-13 loss, and even that felt like an improvement. We'd like to see more improvement in Week 6. Per ESPN, the Saints have a 53.9% chance to pull off the win with just a one-point advantage in simulations. Needless to say, the prediction certainly indicates two evenly matched teams. We may not have reached true must-win territory, but we're getting close. Look for the Saints to bring their best effort in search of their second win of the season.

Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Experts Unanimously Pick Giants to Defeat Saints in Week 6 (Amber Searls-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:26 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants will enter Week 6 of the NFL season holding a record of 3-1-1 following a strange ending last week. The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. The kickoff for the game between the Giants and Saints is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

away.headline: Alvin Kamara’s Injury Playing Status Revealed for Saints RB Depth Chart With Kendre Miller
away.blurb: The New Orleans Saints headed into Sunday waiting to know whether Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave, both listed as questionable, would be available for their Week 6 clash with the New York Giants. #Saints RB Alvin Kamara (back) and WR Chris Olave (illness) are both listed as questionable and both expected to play, sources say. The undrafted rookie CJ Donaldson even out-carried Kamara 4-3 in the loss to the Vikings . Kamara is an incredibly risky play after getting just five touches last week. It's hard to trust that he'll just play the whole game and make plays while he's out there. He has slightly more value in a PPR format, if you don't have any better options. Alvin Kamara's Injury Playing Status Revealed for Saints RB Depth Chart With Kendre Miller Unlock the latest Heavy on Saints news — direct to your inbox. Olave was dealing with an illness, but indications are that he'll play. The news is good on Kamara, too, although it's the kind of news that complicates things in the backfield for New Orleans. Kamara is “expected to play,” according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 18, 2026 Kamara's back injury is something that popped up for the first time on the injury report heading into Week 5, and he was active last week. However, Kamara only got three carries a week ago and pretty much vanished from the game in the second half, so this isn't cut and dry. It'll also be worth checking the Saints' injury report 90 minutes before the game (11:30 a.m. ET injury report, 10:30 a.m. Central) to confirm Kamara's status. Even if he plays, though, things might not be totally straightforward. On paper, the No. 1 spot on this depth chart now appears up for grabs. It previously belonged to Travis Etienne, who is currently on injured reserve. It then went from Etienne to Kamara once Etienne was on IR. But last week, Kamara took a backseat to Kendre Miller, who had 10 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown. That would suggest that Miller is actually ahead of Kamara this week, especially given the veteran is dealing with a potentially nagging back injury, but there's nothing that can just tell us that for certain.
