LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? Sign up to wager on NFL games using the BetMGM bonus code CBSSPORTS to get up to $1,500 in bonus bets: It's starting to cool down around the country, and that will be the case Sunday afternoon in the City of Brotherly Love, via weather.com: Sunny skies. High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. Expert picks for Eagles vs. Panthers in NFL Week 6 action Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts during the first half | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer: Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:13 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first victory of the season last week, but must go on a winning streak in order to make it meaningful. At 1-4, the Bucs are only 1.5 games behind the Carolina Panthers in the weak NFC South division. However, Tampa must win a few more games before it can even start thinking about making the playoffs. Luckily, the Bucs have winnable games on the schedule over the next few weeks, including a pair against division rivals. However, Tampa has the Pittsburgh Steelers on the docket next, already the Bucs' third game against an AFC North foe. The Steelers are 3-2 and have been inconsistent this season, although their offense has turned a corner after a very slow start. The Bucs are 2.5-point underdogs at home, but managed to pull off the upset against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 as 9.5-point underdogs. Beating the Steelers will qualify as an upset, but it is a very winnable game for the Bucs. Aside from a non-existent pass rush, the Bucs' defense has been very good this season. Now it must contend with a red-hot Aaron Rodgers, who has thrown for three TDs in each of Pittsburgh's last three games. Steelers' RB Jaylen Warren has also been outstanding in the last three games, rushing for 127, 93, and 101 yards. He also caught an 80-yard TD last week, and his 230 receiving yards lead the team. Tampa's run defense is second in the NFL so far, and stopping Warren is one of my five keys to a Bucs' victory , as is finally getting the pass rush to show a pulse. On offense, the Bucs have a budding star in RB Bucky Irving, who is coming off a career-best 165 rushing yards and had both a rushing and a receiving TD against Dallas. For Tampa to win, Irving must continue to be the centerpiece of the offense. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be making his third straight start while starting QB Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb. Daniels has played with the poise of a seasoned veteran and earned the first victory of his career against the Cowboys. For Tampa to win, Daniels must once again play a clean, turnover-free game. The offensive line must keep Pittsburgh's pass rush, especially T.J. Watt, away from Daniels. This game is set to be a matchup of strengths against strengths. Warren is sixth in the NFL in rushing yards and will be going up against Tampa's strong run defense. Rodgers has been great over the last three weeks, but will have to make plays against a secondary that has shut down the star WR duos of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Steelers will be without WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson in this game. If Irving can get going early, it will make life much easier for Daniels, whose ability to also make plays with his legs can be a huge factor, especially on third down. This game seems like it could go either way, with a turnover or missed kick looming large at game's end. I don't think it will be Chase McLaughlin who misses the kick, as he has been perfect this season for the Bucs. Prediction: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 22

away.headline: Report: Former Steelers RB Cordarrelle Patterson Arrested For Domestic Assault
away.blurb: Patterson played for the Steelers in 2024, his final stop in the NFL. The four-time Pro Bowler and seven-time All-Pro selection played 12 years and finished his career with the most kickoffs returned for touchdowns with nine, plus the longest kick return for a touchdown of 109 yards. As a kick returner, Patterson struggled. The two-time kick return yards leader only had 11 returns in 2024, totaling 240 yards. He was among the NFL's worst, averaging just 21.8 yards per return. Last season, Pittsburgh replaced Patterson with running back Jaylen Warren and Kenny Gainwell. Gainwell led the team with 26 returns for 633 yards, averaging 24.3 yards per return. He was eventually named the Team MVP after the season. Steelers On SI will continue to release updates as more information on Patterson's arrest becomes available. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who's handled a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence. home.headline: Buccaneers running back's status remains uncertain for Week 6
home.blurb: "We've got to work him out Sunday. That'll be a game-time [decision]," Bowles said. Tucker did not participate in Wednesday's practice and returned in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday. He carries a questionable designation on the final injury report , leaving Tampa Bay uncertain about its backfield rotation. Through five weeks, Tucker has appeared in four games, recording eight carries for 28 yards and one touchdown, according to NFL.com . While his opportunities have been limited, three of his eight rushing attempts have produced first downs, highlighting his situational contributions. With rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels preparing for another start, the Buccaneers will look to maintain that rushing production against Pittsburgh. Tucker's availability could affect how Tampa Bay handles short-yardage situations, although his limited workload makes it difficult to project a significant change in the overall offensive approach. According to the Buccaneers' Friday press conference , head coach Todd Bowles confirmed that Tucker's availability will be determined before kickoff. Tucker scored his first touchdown of the season against Green Bay in Week 4, finishing with 10 yards on three carries. He followed that performance with five carries for 18 yards against Dallas, as Tampa Bay rushed for 241 yards in its first victory of the season. L.A. remains near the top of the odds in the Super Bowl market, but a few injuries – and some close losses – have dropped the Rams to 2-3 and in third place in the NFC West. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to Buffalo at home, yet it’s favored by double digits in this divisional battle with Jacoby Brissett and Co. The Cardinals shocked the NFL world in Week 1, upsetting the Los Angeles Chargers, but the Chargers’ 0-5 start has taken a little away from that victory. Since then, Arizona has lost four straight games, allowing over 30 points in all of them. Plus, the team traded away former top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Houston Texans. At some point, it feels like rookie Carson Beck will get a chance under center, as the Cards are destined for a top-five pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. So, do the Rams take care of business and cover at home? All season long, the SI Betting team is predicting the final score of every NFL game. It’s an exciting exercise that we hope will help guide bettors on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, there’s a chance that we’ll hit an exact score in the process! As the Rams look to get back over .500, they are in desperate need of a get-right game against a weak division opponent. Here’s my final score prediction for this NFC West clash in Week 6. Earlier this week, he explained why he’s betting on Arizona to cover the spread: The Rams have a glaring issue that cost them on Monday Night Football, and it's something that leads me to be cautious about betting on them to cover big spreads: their special teams. It's the worst special teams in the league and has been for the past couple of years. If they make another blunder in Week 6, it's going to tee the Cardinals up to at least cover this big point spread. The Cardinals' defense is one of the worst in the NFL, but they have enough weapons on offense that they should be able to be at least somewhat effective in this game against a Rams team on a short week. I'll take the points with Arizona. I see where MacMillan is coming from with this bet, but the Cardinals have been blown out by Seattle and Detroit this season, and their offense may struggle against a Rams defense that remains a top-five unit against the pass (fourth in EPA/Pass) in 2026. I expect this high-powered Rams attack to push 40 points in Week 6, and I’m not buying this Jacoby Brissett-led offense to put up enough points to cover on the road. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Week 6 Preview: Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Roberts, Editor Toussaint Fancher Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:30 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a disappointing end to Week 5 , the Los Angeles Rams look to get back in the win column against the Arizona Cardinals. "I love Mike [LaFleur], and it's about the Rams versus the Cardinals, and we're going to try to get after him as good as we can this week," Rams head coach Sean McVay said about facing the Cardinals. The Rams will face the Cardinals in the first matchup against former Los Angeles offensive coordinator, Mike LaFleur. LaFleur spent the past two seasons as the Rams' offensive coordinator, and now they will face off for the first time since LaFleur became Arizona's head coach. Last week, the Los Angeles Rams had a great offensive game. The offense was electric as the game became a barnburner. Buffalo and their quarterback Josh Allen were unstoppable on the ground and got the best of the Los Angeles defense. This week, the Rams face the Arizona Cardinals, who are currently 1-4 and on a three-game losing streak. While the Rams must approach every game with the same level of preparation, the Cardinals are an easier opponent than the Bills. Although the Cardinals are an easier matchup, they still have plenty of playmakers. Michael Wilson, Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride are a few of their top tier players who can change the game at a moment's notice. The Cardinals quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, is an experienced veteran who can play his best at any moment. Last season, the journeyman threw for over 3,300 yards with 23 touchdowns – both career highs. The Cardinals are a wildcard on any given game, but the Rams should be able to handle Arizona easily. Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis (92) kicks a point after try during the fourth quarter against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images After the Week 5 loss to the Bills, the Rams made big changes, specifically to the special teams unit. Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis after his poor performance. Mevis missed a 50-yard field attempt and also had a game leading 48-yard field goal blocked in overtime. Rams also released returner and wide receiver Xavier Smith – marred by his costly turnover in the NFC championship game last season. The Rams signed Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad as a replacement. Last season, he played for the Indianapolis Colts and the New Orleans Saints, going 29 for 37 with a long of 60 yards. The Rams' special teams has been the league's worst under McVay since he became head coach. McVay stood behind his special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone after the loss. "I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone," said McVay on Tuesday. "There are no changes that are going to be made there. We're going to keep working. This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of." Following Monday Night's game, the NFL suspended Rams starting left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb. Jackson appealed and his suspension was reduced to one game. Jackson will miss this week's matchup against the Cardinals before returning next week against the Las Vegas Raiders. While no players have been listed out for the game, several were on the injury report or missed practice this week. Tight end Davis Allen was listed as Did Not Participate (DNP) due to a foot injury, and Omar Speights, Nate Landman, Colby Parkinson and Kam Curl were all limited participants. The Last Word Even though the Rams are 2-3, they are still in a good place. The next five games are all winnable, they must remain focused on their opponent each week. The Rams have started 2-3 or worse in four of their six seasons with quarterback Matthew Stafford. In 2023, the Rams started 2-3 and the following year saw a 1-4 start. Despite the slow starts, the Rams made the playoffs in both seasons. The Rams are also waiting on the return of Myles Garrett to pair his extraordinary talents with Aaron Donald. The Rams still have a tough task ahead and need to focus on coming away with a victory on Sunday. away.headline: Trent McDuffie's Late Addition to Rams Injury Report Raises Concern Ahead of Week 6 vs. Cardinals
away.source: Los Angeles Rams On SI on MSN
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams should be as healthy as they've been all season as they enter Week 6 . Only two players will enter Sunday’s game with an injury designation. Safety Kam Curl is officially listed as questionable as he was downgraded from being limited to a non-participant on Friday. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report and is listed as questionable with a groin injury. “Trent felt a little something in his groin so we're going to be smart with him,” said head coach Sean McVay. “He'll be listed as questionable, but he has the right mindset and mentality and we'll just see where we're at with that.” After being a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, tight end Davis Allen was limited on Friday. McVay noted that Allen was trending in the right direction, and the lack of a game designation would seem to imply that he will be available to play. Despite Curl not participating on Friday, McVay also said that he felt good about him. On the Cardinals' side, they’ll be without rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, which will be a hit to their offense and overall explosiveness. Love did not practice with an ankle injury all week and will be officially listed as out. The Cardinals will also be without safeties Wydett Williams and Andrew Wingard. Additionally, safety Kitan Crawford (ankle), safety Budda Baker (rest), linebacker Zaven Collins (hip), and punter Blake Gilikin (back) will all be listed as questionable. Over the last few weeks, the Rams have dealt with their share of injuries. However, they are finally starting to get healthy at the right time. For now, the Rams will have most of their key contributors available against the Cardinals as they look to get back on track. Despite McDuffie not participating in practice on Friday, the Rams don’t seem too concerned about his status going forward. McVay noted that the Rams were simply being smart with McDuffie and that it was just some soreness from the game that he felt ahead of practice. Much like every team in the NFL at this point in the season, the Rams have their bumps and bruises, but for the most part are pretty healthy. The Rams could get another boost in the coming weeks as Myles Garrett works his way back from injury . The Rams did not open Garrett’s practice window this week, but it could be something they look to do following Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. “We've just taken it a week at a time so whenever we connect on Monday, I'll have that answer for you,” said McVay. “He has a good look in his eye and he's making good progress so we'll see.” Rams Injury Report Brings Much-Needed Good News Ahead of Week 6 vs. Cardinals Sunday Morning Rams Notebook: Sean McVay Linked to Amazon, Myles Garrett Update, and More Rams Midweek Report: Searching for Consistency, Myles Garrett Update, Trade Deadline Outlook Rams Midweek Report: Favorable Schedule Ahead, Myles Garrett Update, Sean McVay Concerns Rams vs. Cardinals Week 6 Prediction:

away.blurb: It is not yet clear whether Love’s injury will affect his availability in Week 7, when the Cardinals return home to face the Denver Broncos. When asked whether Love could be placed on injured reserve, LaFleur said “there’s been no discussion of IR or anything like that.” “He's doing good but it's just — you guys see the way he cuts,” LaFleur said. “He cuts hard. That's a superpower of his. And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right, right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants.” Earlier in the week, LaFleur said that Love’s limited involvement as a receiver was because the Cardinals needed their running backs to stay back in pass protection against the Lions. On Friday, he acknowledged that was only a partial truth. Amid a slow start to his rookie season, Love will miss the Arizona Cardinals ' Week 6 trip to face the Los Angeles Rams due to an injury to his left ankle, head coach Mike LaFleur said on Friday, Oct. 16. Love has not practiced all week after experiencing lingering discomfort in recent games. “We knew on Monday after watching the game, talking with him, seeing where he was at, that we were gonna give him Wednesday off,” LaFleur said. “And re-assess on Wednesday, with knowing that probably Sunday was a long shot.” “We've gotta really re-evaluate, really every single day,” LaFleur added. “Not good enough, obviously, right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him. And then we'll re-evaluate, obviously, on Monday.” Love suffered a high-ankle sprain to his right ankle on Aug. 13, in a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders. He returned to the field a month later in the Cardinals’ regular-season opener. Then, at some point in the ensuing weeks, he began to experience discomfort in his left ankle. The issue first drew public attention in Week 4, against the New York Giants. During that game, trainers repeatedly looked at Love’s ankle on the Cardinals sideline. Afterward, Love acknowledged that the Cardinals have been managing his workload due to health. LaFleur, though, was unsure of exactly when the issue first surfaced. "We just felt like it wasn't improving and maybe even getting a little bit worse," LaFleur said. "So at that point, if it's not improving and it's getting a little bit worse, we've gotta do what's right for the player." Through five games, Love has just 245 rushing yards on 67 carries, for a 3.7 yards per carry average. Love has also caught just 11 passes on 14 targets for 36 yards, falling far short of the expectations with he entered the NFL as a pass-catcher. Over the Cardinals’ past two games, he ran just 20 total routes. “To run routes and separate, you've gotta be able to put those feet in the ground,” LaFleur said. “And it's gotta be deliberate. away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.headline: New Trent McDuffie injury could shake up Rams secondary yet again
home.blurb: For a second straight week, the Los Angeles Rams' final injury report is thankfully sparse. The headliner in Week 6 is star cornerback Trent McDuffie, a late addition after tweaking his groin in practice, per head coach Sean McVay. McDuffie sat out Friday's session and his status for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals could be in jeopardy. Safety Kam Curl, another Friday DNP, is also questionable with an ankle injury, but McVay said he "feels good" about his status for the game. If McDuffie misses, that means more Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in coverage. Where have we heard that before? The Rams encountered a similar scenario with Jaylen Watson out for the second half in Week 3 against the Broncos and in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. In addition to Watson, the defense also played multiple games without safety Kamren Kinchens, who strained his hamstring in Week 1 and sat out until the Eagles game. Although Curl hasn't missed a game, he's been nursing that ankle injury all year. The other starting safety, Quentin Lake, was questionable entering Week 5 before suiting up to play. Wallace has played well and, based on how the Rams handled Watson's absence, would replace McDuffie as the second starter on the outside. Aside from a very poor showing in Denver, Forbes has also performed decently in limited reps. Relying on those two against Arizona would not be the end of the world. For whatever reason, this Rams secondary can't seem to stay healthy. Rams will call on Wallace and Forbes if Trent McDuffie misses McDuffie, one of the NFL's top corners this season, would be the biggest loss by far, and late injury-report additions tend to bode poorly. "He's got the right mentality and mindset and we'll kind of just see where we're at," McVay said of McDuffie's chances to play. The other part, of course, is that it's against Arizona , who just traded former first-round receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and will also miss rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) this week against the Rams. The Cardinals' top receiving threat is tight end Trey McBride, which is more a problem for linebackers Nate Landman and Omar Speights and Lake as a nickel. McBride is only averaging 7.3 yards per catch, anyway, and Arizona's lead wideout Michael Wilson, while providing a productive 57.6 yards per contest, is averaging just 9.9. WR2 Kendrick Bourne might actually be the bigger concern for LA; with the San Francisco 49ers, meeting last season, an overtime win for 'Zona, Bourne erupted for 10 catches and 142 yards. Rams' Josh Wallace keeps proving himself at every opportunity Cardinals' Marvin Harrison Jr. trade benefits Rams in multiple ways 4 struggling teams the Rams should watch as trade deadline nears Rams' reluctance to test drafted rookies isn't helping the near future Final injury report vs. Bills gives Rams their most clarity in weeks This article was originally published on ramblinfan.com as New Trent McDuffie injury could shake up Rams secondary yet again .

away.headline: Never had a sophisticated offense — Cris Carter calls out Jim Harbaugh over lack of NFL success amid Chargers’ 2026 struggles
away.blurb: Harbaugh’s offensive struggles cannot be separated from the Chargers’ injury problems. More than half of the team’s original 53-man roster has either landed on Injured Reserve or appeared on weekly injury reports, leaving the coaching staff with limited options at several positions. Such an inexperienced unit has made it difficult to provide Herbert with consistent protection. The constant pressure and changes along the line have also limited the offense’s ability to establish a rhythm. The Los Angeles Chargers have endured a nightmare start to the 2026 NFL season, raising serious questions about Jim Harbaugh’s approach. Their 23-17 loss to the Denver Broncos, after surrendering a 17-10 lead late in the game, dropped them to 0-5, their worst start since 2003. The Chargers’ offense has been one of their biggest problems, averaging just 17 points per game while struggling to find consistency amid a growing list of injuries. Quarterback Justin Herbert has also endured a difficult stretch, recording 937 passing yards, five total touchdowns, seven interceptions, and six fumbles through five games. With the team struggling to find answers, Pro Football Hall of Famer Cris Carter has questioned whether Harbaugh’s offensive approach is the right fit for Herbert. Cris Carter Questions Harbaugh’s Offensive System Speaking on the “Inside Football” podcast, Carter raised concerns about Harbaugh’s history of developing quarterbacks and building an effective passing offense in the NFL. “When has Jim Harbaugh had a very effective passing game in the National Football League?” Carter asked. The former wide receiver acknowledged Harbaugh’s success with creative running schemes and dual-threat quarterbacks, particularly during his time with the San Francisco 49ers. However, he believes Harbaugh has yet to build an offense that fully takes advantage of a quarterback with Herbert’s arm talent. “He’s never had someone who had the talent of Justin Herbert, arm talent in the pocket, and he has never had a sophisticated offense to go with any of the teams,” Carter said. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Carter also questioned whether the system Harbaugh used successfully at the college level can produce the same results in the NFL. “My concern is not only for Justin Herbert, his growth, but this is not a great marriage,” he said. “Even though Harbaugh has proven himself as being a very good coach, he has not taken quarterbacks to the next level.” Injuries Have Made Justin Herbert’s Job Even Harder The offensive line has been hit particularly hard. Los Angeles started four rookies up front in Week 5, with Travis Burke at left tackle, Logan Taylor at left guard, Jake Slaughter at center, and Alex Harkey at right tackle. Veteran Cole Strange filled the right guard position. Herbert’s struggles are reflected in his PFN NFL QB Impact Grade of 60.6, which ranks last among 34 eligible quarterbacks, highlighting just how difficult his start to the season has

away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Speaking to the media on Friday afternoon, Chiefs HC Andy Reid ruled out WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) and LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 6. Rice did not participate in practice this week; however, he was seen on the sideline coaching up second-year WR Jalen Royals. Simmons was a limited participant all week, which Coach Reid said was intentional. "Yeah, he got some work," Reid said. "He didn't work in the team periods, but that was the idea that we went out with, just so we could get some base in there with some fundamentals and technique and start getting that back." Simmons continues to make incremental strides toward returning after missing practically two months with a bulging disc in his back. "Yeah, he was excited to be out there," Reid said of Simmons. "Just be back with the guys and out there on the field, instead of the meeting room." Here's a quick breakdown of each team's final Week 6 injury report, including game-status designations. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related The Chiefs are listing CB L'Jarius Sneed as questionable with his knee injury. It's a constant battle, and this week it seems to be giving him more trouble than not. Chiefs HC Andy Reid on whether Rashee Rice would be available for Week 7: "Yeah, I mean, you guys saw him out there. He's out there and wanting to jump in on everything, and he'll be all right. You never know about these (hamstring injuries), but he's a pretty fast healer." home.headline: Ahead of Chiefs matchup, wounded, winless Chargers share lengthy injury report
home.blurb: Included in the list of injured players were starting left tackle Joe Alt (neck, DNP), star safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring, DNP) and leading wide receivers Ladd McConkey (foot, limited participant) and Quentin Johnston (chest, limited). At wide receiver, Los Angeles is dealing with a plethora of issues. In addition to McConkey and Johnston’s ailments, Tre’ Harris (hamstring, DNP), Brenen Thompson (quadriceps, limited), and former Chief Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib, limited) were listed on Wednesday’s report. Skip to content Best Deals KC KCTV Tower 3 Degree Guarantee MyKC Live It’s Your Health Advertise With Us Jobs KCTV5 Cares Choices, Hope, and Science Watch Live First Warn 5 Weather 7-Day Forecast Station Information Meet the Team KANSAS CITY, Mo. (KCTV) - A wounded and winless Los Angeles Chargers team is headed toward Kansas City this weekend looking to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad. Kansas City and Los Angeles kick off Sunday’s game at 3:25 p.m. CT. It can be watched live in Kansas City and the surrounding viewing area on KCTV5.

They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3. Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8. Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. away.headline: Bills face DJ Moore dilemma despite positive sign before Raiders clash
away.blurb: The Buffalo Bills have offered a positive sign over DJ Moore's availability for a clash with the Las Vegas Raiders, but there is still uncertainty over whether the wide receiver will return. Moore missed Buffalo's win over the Los Angeles Rams with a lingering shoulder injury. The issue also forced him out of the second half of the previous week's defeat to the New England Patriots. Buffalo Bills' roster decision offers hope over DJ Moore return That is a notable change from last week, when Buffalo brought up wide receiver and special teams regular Trent Sherfield. His elevation was an early indication that Moore would be unavailable against the Rams. Capaccio also suggested the Bills could take a cautious approach with Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver, who was also listed as questionable on the final injury report. Moore's desire to play may not be enough to secure his return. Buffalo's final decision will depend on whether he is healthy enough to contribute against the Raiders. The Bills did not elevate any players from their practice squad for the next game, according to The Athletic's Joe Buscaglia . With no additional receiver called up this time, there is reason to believe Moore could be back in the line-up. However, the roster decision does not confirm that he will play. Buffalo struggled to get its passing game going early against the Rams, leaving Josh Allen to improvise when his receivers could not get open. Allen responded with a strong second half and overtime, finishing with 121 rushing yards, a rushing touchdown and a passing touchdown. Despite the encouraging signs, WGR 550 reporter Sal Capaccio believes the Bills could decide against rushing Moore back. "My feeling is no. Not playing, that's my feeling, that he wouldn't play," Capaccio said of Moore. "He wants to play. We know that, right? He wants to play, that's just in his nature." The Bills managed to beat the Rams without Moore and scored 37 points in the process. With a bye week coming up, they have an opportunity to give the receiver extra time to recover rather than risk aggravating his shoulder injury. Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play." Moore missed Buffalo's win over the Los Angeles Rams with a lingering shoulder injury. The issue also forced him out of the second half of the previous week's defeat to the New England Patriots. Buffalo Bills' roster decision offers hope over DJ Moore return That is a notable change from last week, when Buffalo brought up wide receiver and special teams regular Trent Sherfield. His elevation was an early indication that Moore would be unavailable against the Rams. Capaccio also suggested the Bills could take a cautious approach with Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver, who was also listed as questionable on the final injury report. Moore's desire to play may not be enough to secure his return. Buffalo's final decision will depend on whether he is healthy enough to contribute against the Raiders. Bills face DJ Moore dilemma despite positive sign before Raiders clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Bills face DJ Moore dilemma despite positive sign before Raiders clash Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Aryan Chadha Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:30 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Bills are coming off a 37-point performance against the Rams and will have a bye week after facing Las Vegas, giving them a chance to prioritise Moore's recovery if he is not fully fit. The Bills did not elevate any players from their practice squad for the next game, according to The Athletic's Joe Buscaglia . With no additional receiver called up this time, there is reason to believe Moore could be back in the line-up. However, the roster decision does not confirm that he will play. Buffalo struggled to get its passing game going early against the Rams, leaving Josh Allen to improvise when his receivers could not get open. Allen responded with a strong second half and overtime, finishing with 121 rushing yards, a rushing touchdown and a passing touchdown. Despite the encouraging signs, WGR 550 reporter Sal Capaccio believes the Bills could decide against rushing Moore back. "My feeling is no. Not playing, that's my feeling, that he wouldn't play," Capaccio said of Moore. "He wants to play. We know that, right? He wants to play, that's just in his nature." The Bills managed to beat the Rams without Moore and scored 37 points in the process. With a bye week coming up, they have an opportunity to give the receiver extra time to recover rather than risk aggravating his shoulder injury. home.headline: Bills vs. Raiders injury update: Buffalo's injury list grows, Ashton Jeanty banged up
home.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns. NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation. Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return. Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter. He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday. Oliver did not practice at all last week. Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice. Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday. He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. Ashton Jeanty played against New England despite being listed as questionable because of ankle and foot injuries. "Unless I can't run, jump, I'm playing. Football is a tough game. You're never gonna play feeling 100 percent," Jeanty said. "So at the end of the day, I just want to go out there and do my best for my teammates and whatever it takes." He was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Nailor is expected to return to practice this week as he works through the NFL concussion protocol. home.blurb: Bills' Final Week 6 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Four Others Questionable to Face Raiders Skip to main content SI.COM The Buffalo Bills have ruled five players as questionable to face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. One of the 10 without a game designation is starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left the Week 5 win , and did not return, after 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. Brown practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday before improving to full participation on Thursday and Friday. With a minor "muscle freak out" now in the rearview, the starting right tackle is ready for his 79th regular season appearance in a Bills' uniform. In another positive development, running back Ty Johnson, who was limited by a hamstring at the first two practices, participated in full on Friday, and he's been cleared for the Sunday game. DJ Moore, Ed Oliver return to practice Moore and Oliver both sat out the October 12 win over the Los Angeles Rams after injury incidents knocked them out of the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots. Neither player participated at practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but both returned to the field in a limited capacity on Friday, providing a glimmer of hope that they'll be available for kickoff. "They've been doing a lot on the side. They've been doing all the walkthroughs and everything. It was good to get them out here today, and just being able to move around," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady . "We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions. I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play." After being scratched in Week 5, Alford and Palmer logged limited participation all three days this week. The former is nursing a minor ankle issue that emerged against the Patriots. The latter is fighting through a shoulder injury from an October 9 practice. Both Alford and Palmer showed positive signs throughout the week, looking ready to return to game action, by multiple accounts, during media-viewing portions of practice. Sanders, who has already dealt with a knee issue and a subsequent bout with appendicitis, made his season debut on October 12. He performed well over 51 defensive snaps, but apparently came out of the overtime win bothered by a shoulder. He progressed to full participation at Friday's practice, but remains questionable to play. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious. New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers. Cowboys vs. Packers prediction Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams . However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. The Cowboys are averaging 3.07 points per drive, the second-highest by a team under .500 through five games this century per CBS Sports Research, but their 45 drives this season are the second fewest in the league this season. Among the NFL teams that have played in all five weeks of the 2026 season, Dallas' 45 drives stand as the fewest. That's what happens when you have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room.
