Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. Saints won't cover as road favorite at Giants Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL. Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough. Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago. On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Packers: 26 The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air . The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys' front office did this to them. Over a year later, and the debate about whether or not they won the trade that sent superstar edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers rages on. Jerry Jones implored the fanbase that he was in the right, after a contract dispute led to Parsons holding out during 2025 training camp and the exhibition season, leading to him being dealt prior to the start of the regular season. Jones claimed that trading Parsons would lead to the Cowboys' run defense improving and the salary cap savings would lead to a number of improvements elsewhere on the roster. The players acquired (Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Malachi Lawrence) and the cap space allocation (Jake Ferguson, DaRon Bland) have not worked out for the Cowboys in 2026. As for Parsons, he was placed on the PUP list to start the season after missing the end of last year with an ACL tear. He was projected to potentially return this week, as fans circled the Week 6 matchup when the schedules were announced in May. Will he suit up on Sunday Night Football? He will not. Parsons' practice window has not been started by the Packers, meaning he is still at least a couple weeks away from returning. Parsons himself claims that if the Super Bowl was this week he'd play, but he's being cautious to ensure that the common compensation injuries that can result from returning too soon don't impact him when he does return to the field. Parsons remains on the Active/PUP list for Week 6. Initially, Green Bay was seen as being on the better end of the swap, and the two teams met and had a 40-40 tie that left a stalemate on the official ledger. The Packers were seen as the victors, with a 9-3-1 record while Dallas' defense struggled mightily, but a late season Parsons ACL tear started to shift the narrative. Dallas used the draft picks acquired to trade for DT Williams and draft Lawrence in the first round, and spent the extra space to extend Bland and Ferguson. When Williams was extended as the centerpiece of the new-look defense, people started claiming the Cowboys ended up on the better end of the deal. Five weeks into the season the run defense is as bad as ever and most fans want Bland and Ferguson benched. The Packers lot every game down the stretch after Parsons industry and are trying to keep their heads above water entering Week 6 this year. It's safe to say that no one has won the trade thus far. away.headline: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status

away.blurb: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is on track to return to the lineup in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season. Jacobs will be inactive for Week 6, but he is on track to return in Week 7, barring any further discipline. According to Schefter, the league's investigation into Jacobs will remain open, so it reserves the right to discipline the star running back further if necessary. Even though Jacobs has not played yet this season, he is expected to return as the team's starting running back in Week 7, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. Josh Jacobs will immediately return as the Packers’ starting running back next week at Detroit. Meanwhile, Micah Parsons still isn’t ready to practice, making it unlikely he plays before Nov. 8 against the Patriots at the soonest. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/hVvUAJDNjT pic.twitter.com/2M9OZC0qlY Jacobs' eventual return is massive for a Green Bay team that has the fewest rushing yards in the NFL through five weeks. The former first-round pick had a big 2025 season, rushing for 929 yards on 234 carries (4.0 yards per carry) in 15 games. He found the end zone 13 times on the ground, and he added 36 catches (on 44 targets) for 282 yards and an additional score. Is Josh Jacobs Playing Tonight? (Update, Betting Impact for Cowboys vs. Packers in NFL Week 6) Skip to main content ON SI According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, Jacobs will be removed from the league's Commissioner's Exempt List on Monday, following the Packers' Week 6 matchup with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. ESPN sources: Packers RB Josh Jacobs is being removed from the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The investigation will remain open for the NFL so it reserves the right to add further discipline if and when warranted. Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Week 7. pic.twitter.com/sAX0pDV9JT Jacobs has not played in a game in the 2026 season after he was charged with two misdemeanors after a dispute with his ex-girlfriend. Earlier in the year, Jacobs accepted a non contest plea agreement for a misdemeanor charge of battery. "Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," Jacobs' attorneys attorneys Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld told Sports Illustrated in a statement. "He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment." Green Bay has been rolling with Marshawn Lloyd as the team's top back with Jacobs ineligible, and he'll be backed up by Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. in Week 6 with Chris Brooks currently on injured reserve. Lloyd found the end zone twice in Week 5 against the Chicago Bears, and he has a favorable matchup against the Dallas defense, which is No. 32 in the league

home.headline: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report
home.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status

home.headline: Green Bay Packers: NFL insider reveals the new Micah Parsons return target
home.blurb: Hopefully, Green Bay can avoid any more serious injuries. On the positive side, they are expecting to get two key contributors back very soon. It has recently been reported that Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs will return as the starting running back in Week Seven. Additionally, All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons is getting closer and closer to his own return. NFL insider expects Micah Parsons to return in Week 9 for the Green Bay Packers Initially, many hoped that the All-Pro pass rusher would be able to return for Green Bay’s Week Six matchup against his former team. However, the Packers have not opened up his practice window as they want to ensure that he is 100% healthy and not at risk for any soft tissue injuries because of rushing a return to the field. “A league source tells me Parsons might not return until Week 9, against the Patriots on Nov. 8. The Packers did not open his practice window this week to begin his return. In Week 7, Green Bay plays the Detroit Lions before hosting the Panthers on “’Thursday Night Football’; believing Parsons needs more than a week to ramp up, the short-week turnaround would be difficult to pull off.” If this is truly the targeted return date, it would be realistic to see Parsons designated for return by Green Bay this week. This means he would be able to practice with the rest of the team, and the Packers would have 21 days to add him to the active roster. While he will not play in that many games in 2026, Green Bay is hopeful that his return will take their already impressive defense under Jonathan Gannon to an even higher level. The Green Bay Packers have lost several players to season-ending injuries already this year. These include defensive stars Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave as well as offensive stars Zach Tom and Jayden Reed. Despite these losses, and terrible play from their offensive line early in year, Green Bay has gone 3-2 in their first five games. Parsons, who was acquired prior to the start of the 2025 season in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys, tore his ACL in late in the year and has missed every game of 2026 thus far. Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported on Saturday morning that those around the NFL expect Parsons back in Week Nine when Green Bay faces the New England Patriots : Last season, Parsons became the first player in NFL history to record 12+ sacks in each of his first five seasons. He had 12.5 in 14 games played in his first season with the Packers and was named First Team All-Pro. home.blurb: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is on track to return to the lineup in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season. Jacobs will be inactive for Week 6, but he is on track to return in Week 7, barring any further discipline. According to Schefter, the league's investigation into Jacobs will remain open, so it reserves the right to discipline the star running back further if necessary. Even though Jacobs has not played yet this season, he is expected to return as the team's starting running back in Week 7, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. Josh Jacobs will immediately return as the Packers’ starting running back next week at Detroit. Meanwhile, Micah Parsons still isn’t ready to practice, making it unlikely he plays before Nov. 8 against the Patriots at the soonest. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/hVvUAJDNjT pic.twitter.com/2M9OZC0qlY Jacobs' eventual return is massive for a Green Bay team that has the fewest rushing yards in the NFL through five weeks. The former first-round pick had a big 2025 season, rushing for 929 yards on 234 carries (4.0 yards per carry) in 15 games. He found the end zone 13 times on the ground, and he added 36 catches (on 44 targets) for 282 yards and an additional score. Is Josh Jacobs Playing Tonight? The investigation will remain open for the NFL so it reserves the right to add further discipline if and when warranted. Earlier in the year, Jacobs accepted a non contest plea agreement for a misdemeanor charge of battery. "Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," Jacobs' attorneys attorneys Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld told Sports Illustrated in a statement. "He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment." Green Bay has been rolling with Marshawn Lloyd as the team's top back with Jacobs ineligible, and he'll be backed up by Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. in Week 6 with Chris Brooks currently on injured reserve. Lloyd found the end zone twice in Week 5 against the Chicago Bears, and he has a favorable matchup against the Dallas defense, which is No. 32 in the league

picks.headline: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Auburn stuns No. 1 Georgia A.J. Brown coming off IR Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 1:54 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the Washington Commanders are likely playing with a lame-duck coach, the San Francisco 49ers will be without a key defender. These teams, going in different directions, will meet in Week 6 on Monday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Still reeling from a last-second overtime mental meltdown in the 27-27 tie to the Giants, the Commanders carry a record of 1-3-1 and a heavy underdog role into this game. Meanwhile, the 49ers are flying high with a record of 5-0 on the season. They're coming off an exciting 32-29 win over the Seahawks, giving them firm control of the NFC West title chase. 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 300 yards The Commanders have been good against the run this season, giving up only 95.4 yards per game. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. It’s Week 6 and the Washington Commanders are traveling west to play the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. The Commanders are big underdogs in this critical primetime game, and need a win to keep any hope for this season alive. The 49ers are one of three undefeated teams left in the NFL at 5-0, and are considered one of the best team’s in the NFL. The Commanders tied with the Giants last week, putting them at 1-3-1 for the season, and in code red territory before their Week 7 bye. The Niners are coming off a brutal division win over the Seattle Seahawks, the reigning Super Champions, and the only team Washington has a win against this season. San Francisco continues to be one of the most injured teams in the NFL, but they have overcome to stay on top. RBs Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) have also been limited in practice this week. WRs Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs have both been dealing with hamstring injuries. McLaurin played last week, but Diggs didn’t. They’re both expected to play this week, giving Jayden Daniels another target. On one side, it's Washington's Jayden Daniels, a former NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, Heisman Trophy winner and No. 2 overall draft pick who is as much of a dual-threat passer as there is. On the other, it's former Mr. Irrelevant draft choice Brock Purdy for San Francisco, and he might win his first NFL MVP Award this season. Purdy can run a little but is a pocket passer. Unbeaten San Francisco already leads the NFC West by two games and all due respect to fellow 5-0 team Minnesota, the 49ers look like the conference's best team so far. Massive, massive blunder that's probably on QB Jayden Daniels for snapping the ball on the play previous, but he was told to try and gain more yards. So that's on embattled head coach Dan Quinn. Even Commanders minority owner Magic Johnson called out the team on social media. It marked Washington's first time failing to win when leading by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter at home since 1999. away.headline: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL’s ‘Next Great’ Cornerback
away.blurb: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL's ‘Next Great' Cornerback The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants , in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. "SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week." By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. "Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day," The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return." Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 11:27pm Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions . Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Play Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders "Trey Amos has no hobbies," Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. "No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back." Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. "My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. Amos started training camp on the PUP list but returned to practice a few weeks later … and automatically got hurt again. away.headline: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers
away.blurb: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers Skip to main content SI.COM The Washington Commanders' final injury report lists a baker's dozen of players out or questionable, sure to create an availability problem for Washington facing the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Four players are officially listed as out: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee) , and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle). All four players missed practice all week. Nine additional players are also listed as questionable, including Stefon Diggs, Javon Kinlaw, and three safeties. Of the three safeties, Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice but were upgraded to limited; Nick Cross (illness) was a full participant all three days but is still questionable. All three players missed last week's game against New York . Quan Martin improved from limited on Thursday to full participation on Friday and Saturday, with no game designation. Stefon Diggs' return is possible; he's officially listed as questionable. He went from missing Thursday's practice to limited on both Friday and Saturday. Terry McLaurin has no game designation after being limited Thursday and Saturday and sitting out Friday with a hamstring/rest designation. Treylon Burks was also limited all three days but has no game designation. Getting Diggs back would give Jayden Daniels another option in the passing game after playing without him against the Giants. The Commanders will also be without Croskey-Merritt in the backfield , but they should have options. Austin Ekeler was limited all week with a chest injury, while Rachaad White went from full participation Thursday to limited Friday and Saturday. Neither received a game designation. Jeremy McNichols was a full participant all three days but remains questionable with a quad injury. He would also need to be activated from injured reserve before he can play Monday. Washington Commanders PR Washington's defensive front is another area to watch with Omenihu and Jean-Baptiste both out. Kinlaw fully participated Thursday, missed Friday's practice, and returned Saturday on a limited basis. He's questionable with ankle and knee injuries. K'Lavon Chaisson, meanwhile, returned to full participation Saturday after sitting out Friday and has no game designation. There are still a few roster decisions to make before Monday night. Trey Amos (ankle) and Jordan Magee (hamstring) are both questionable and, like McNichols, remain in their 21-day practice windows. Neither can play until they are activated from their respective reserve lists. Lucas Patrick is also questionable with an illness despite returning to full participation Saturday. Washington knows which four players it won't have against San Francisco, but with nine more listed as questionable, the Commanders still have plenty to sort out before Monday night's kickoff. The extra day helps us, and so kind of a fluid situation there." A stomach illness is making the rounds in the locker room, and rookie defensive end Romello Height appears to be the latest to catch it. Evans has been playing through a rib injury, while the Achilles issue is new. Head coach Kyle Shanahan described it as "soreness." Defensive tackle Gracen Halton missed his second consecutive practice with a quadriceps injury. Like Evans, he was seen working on the side Friday. home.blurb: Game status | Jacory Croskey-Merritt ruled out vs. 49ers Skip to main content Primary nav SEASON TICKETS Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has been ruled out of the Washington Commanders' Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Saturday. Croskey-Merritt, who leads the team in rushing yards, is dealing with a groin injury that has kept him out of practice all week. Croskey-Merritt re-injured the same groin that has nagged him in recent weeks, Quinn said. Jeremy McNichols, who started the season on Injured Reserve, had a full week of practice and could return to the active roster this weekend. McNichols would likely be the third running back in the rotation, but the Commanders like the versatility and professionalism he brings to the position. Javontae Jean-Baptiste, Charles Omenihu and Marcus Mariota were also ruled out for Monday's game. The rest of the players, including Injured Reserve players like Trey Amos and other key players on the injury report like Nick Cross, will all travel to California. Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season saw the Washington Commanders host the New York Giants, while the Dallas Cowboys hosted the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football. The Philadelphia Eagles headed to London to duke it out with the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday morning. news Commanders vs. 49ers preview | A trip out west news Jayden Daniels looked like himself in return The Commanders have other options at running back with Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler on the roster. White has carried the ball 29 times for 118 yards, averaging 4.1 yards per carry. White also adds a dimension to the passing game, as he has caught all 10 of his targets for 53 yards and a touchdown. "He can make a cut and make big plays on that," Quinn said of White. Ekeler, who signed with the team prior to the Commanders' game against the Indianapolis Colts, was thrown into the rotation during his first game. He carried the ball four times for 29 yards in London, showing off some of the quickness and vision that enticed Washington when he first signed with the team three seasons ago. "His explosiveness in the passing game is a big deal," Quinn said. "So, having some combination of the guys, I think that's what we'll lean on most right now." The team will decide whether to activate McNichols on Monday. "He's had a very good week," Quinn said.
